response:
Diagnosis driving this batch. Two lessons from the archive: (i) level-of-investment sorts (TangibilityWeightedCapacityGrowth, PhysicalExpansionInNonInnovators, ExternalCapitalRaisedByNonInnovators) produce strong FMB slopes but no FF5 alpha — CMA absorbs or inverts them, so multiplicative "growth × intangible-deficit gate" structures are a dead end for portfolio evidence; (ii) the only real FF5 alpha so far came from a *sourcing-mix* composition variable (BuyVersusBuildInnovation, alpha −4.7%, t −2.6) whose FMB slope was killed by boundary mass points and 0.075 coverage (uncoalesced aqc, no capex leg). A third clue: the one gross-profit-scaled signal (InventoryBuildPerGrossProfit) was the best joint performer among the flow signals, suggesting pricing-power scaling rather than asset scaling keeps investment signals from collapsing into CMA. This batch repairs the mix family's coverage/continuity, tests gross-profit scaling explicitly, and adds two structurally new constructions (strategy-persistence counts, distance-from-own-peak substitution) that fix the NaN/scale-dominance failure of the substitution index.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: AcquiredShareOfThreeYearInvestment
EXPRESSION: RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(aqc, 0), 3), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(aqc, 0), 3), ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Holding the size of the three-year investment program fixed, the fraction executed by buying other firms rather than building plant and knowledge internally predicts lower returns, because acquired capability is paid for at market prices while internally built capital is acquired at cost.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This repairs the two defects that broke BuyVersusBuildInnovation's cross-sectional slope: aqc is coalesced to zero (missing acquisition spend is economically "no acquisitions", not a missing observation) and three-year sums plus a capex leg smooth the lumpiness that pushed observations onto the 0/1 boundaries, so coverage should roughly double and the ranking becomes continuous. The mechanism is unchanged from the one construction that produced a reliable FF5 alpha, so this is a targeted attempt to make the FMB and portfolio evidence agree.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: AcquirerYearsMinusInnovatorYears
EXPRESSION: SUB(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(aqc, 0), at), 0.02), 5), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 0.02), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: What is priced is the firm's persistent growth strategy, not any single year's spending: serial acquirers who repeatedly buy capability and never sustain a research program underperform firms that show a persistent commitment to internal knowledge investment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Counting the number of years out of five in which the firm was a material acquirer versus a material R&D spender converts both channels into commensurable, unit-free frequencies, so neither leg's dollar magnitude can dominate the other — the flaw that made the earlier substitution numerator a disguised PPE-change sort. It also tests a distinct mechanism, strategy persistence rather than current-year mix, and its discrete support spreads firms across many populated buckets rather than boundary spikes.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: CapexPerDollarOfGrossProfit
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(MA(RATIO(capx, SUB(sale, cogs)), 3), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Physical investment is only value-creating when the firm has intangible pricing power to monetize the capacity; firms that must spend heavily on plant relative to the gross profit their products earn are commodity operators whose capital deployment earns no economic rent.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Scaling investment by gross profit rather than by assets was the feature of the archive's best-behaved flow signal, and it changes the economics: the sort ranks capital intensity relative to product-market rents instead of ranking investment level, which should keep it from being neutralized by CMA the way asset-scaled expansion signals were. Three-year averaging targets the persistent capital-intensity state rather than lumpy annual capex.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: PlantMinusKnowledgeSpendPerGrossProfit
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(SUB(sale, cogs), 3)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Among firms with equal pricing power, those whose investment budget tilts toward plant and away from knowledge are deploying capital into replicable capacity, and this tilt predicts lower returns than an equally sized knowledge-tilted budget.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This is deliberately the same scaling as Signal 3 with the knowledge leg netted out, so the pair isolates whether the intangible dimension adds predictive content beyond capital intensity itself — a design question the archive cannot currently answer. Both legs are annual spending flows of comparable magnitude for R&D-reporting firms, so unlike the flagged ΔR&D-minus-ΔPPE construction the numerator is not mechanically dominated by one channel.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: BoughtVersusBuiltCapitalBase
EXPRESSION: RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: The share of a firm's economic capital that was purchased at a premium (goodwill) rather than built through cumulative capex and research reflects capital acquired above replacement cost, and such capital generates lower future returns and carries impairment exposure.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This is the stock counterpart to Signal 1's flow mix, so the pair identifies whether the buy-versus-build effect is a slow-moving balance-sheet state or a recent-transaction effect — a cleaner test than the archived goodwill signal, which failed on the FMB side because it multiplied goodwill share by a noisy revenue-growth gate. Goodwill is coalesced to zero because absence of goodwill genuinely means no purchased capital, and the denominator's organic investment stock keeps the ratio bounded and comparable across sizes.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: PeakRelativeKnowledgeVersusPlantSpending
EXPRESSION: SUB(COALESCE(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), TS_MAX(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), 0), RATIO(capx, TS_MAX(capx, 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms sustaining knowledge investment at its own five-year peak while physical investment has fallen well below its peak are reallocating toward intangible capital, and because the R&D leg is expensed while the retrenched capex leg looks like contraction, the market underreacts to the transition.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Normalizing each channel by its own five-year maximum puts both legs on a common [0,1] scale, which repairs both failures of the earlier substitution index: the variance can no longer be dominated by the larger physical flow, and the signal varies continuously instead of collapsing onto ±1 and producing an undefined long-short spread. The distance-from-own-peak construction is also a new mechanism in the archive — it measures retrenchment relative to a firm's own history rather than cross-sectional intensity, so it is close to industry- and scale-neutral.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---CRITIQUE AcquiredShareOfThreeYearInvestment---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A legitimate and mechanically motivated repair of the archived buy-versus-build ratio (broader denominator, smoothing, coalesced aqc), but the stated cure for boundary spikes is self-contradictory — coalescing missing aqc to zero *creates* a large point mass at exactly 0 — and the dropped ABS lets negative/divestiture aqc push the ratio outside [0,1], so it risks being an acquisition-intensity (known acquirer-underperformance) sort with a degenerate short leg.

---CRITIQUE AcquirerYearsMinusInnovatorYears---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Persistence-counting is a genuinely different mechanism from current-year mix and the unit-free frequency legs fix the scale-domination problem, but R&D reporting status is extremely sticky so the second term will be near-binary (0 or 5) for most firms, meaning much of the variation is a re-labelled "no-R&D firm" dummy — a well-documented effect — rather than a new acquirer-versus-innovator contrast.

---CRITIQUE CapexPerDollarOfGrossProfit---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Cross-sectionally capx/(sale−cogs) is approximately (capx/at)÷(gross profit/at), i.e. a mechanical ratio of two canonical published anomalies — the capex/investment anomaly (Titman-Wei-Xie) in the numerator and gross profitability (Novy-Marx) in the denominator — both signed the same way, so a negative slope would be a rediscovery rather than evidence for the stated pricing-power mechanism, and the claim that gross-profit scaling escapes CMA is asserted without argument.

---CRITIQUE PlantMinusKnowledgeSpendPerGrossProfit---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: With xrd coalesced to zero, this collapses exactly to Signal 3 for the majority of firms that report no R&D, and for the rest capex typically dominates R&D outside pharma/software, so it is largely a cosmetic variant of the previous proposal whose residual variation is driven by R&D-reporting status rather than the claimed equal-pricing-power tilt; the paired "design test" it promises is therefore not identified.

---CRITIQUE BoughtVersusBuiltCapitalBase---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A coherent stock-based complement to the flow mix that avoids the archived signal's noisy revenue gate, but the numerator is a lifetime cumulative stock while the denominator is only a three-year flow sum, so the ratio mechanically increases with firm age and acquisition history and overlaps substantially with known goodwill-intensity/post-merger underperformance evidence; a large point mass at zero for non-acquirers also weakens the short leg.

---CRITIQUE PeakRelativeKnowledgeVersusPlantSpending---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Normalizing each channel by its own five-year peak is a genuinely new, scale- and industry-neutral construction that plausibly fixes the undefined spread of the archived substitution index, but the COALESCE(...,0) on the R&D leg assigns all non-R&D firms a value in [−1,0], so the short side is again contaminated by R&D-reporting status, and both legs cluster near 1 for growing firms, likely thinning the extreme buckets.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: CapacityPushAgainstMarginErosion
EXPRESSION: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: Capacity expansion is only justified when the product-market rents that intangible advantages generate are holding up; a firm pushing physical investment to the top of its own five-year range while its gross margin sits at the bottom of its own five-year range is expanding into a commoditizing business and will disappoint.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Both legs are within-firm time-series percentile positions, which removes the cross-sectional level of capex intensity and the cross-sectional level of gross profitability — precisely the two published anomaly components the critic identified in the ratio form — leaving only the timing interaction between capacity investment and margin erosion. Because the construct is a difference of two [0,1] own-history ranks, it is scale-, industry- and level-neutral, so it cannot be mechanically absorbed by CMA or RMW, and both tails are populated by real cohorts (expanding commoditizers versus retrenching margin-improvers).

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: ShiftTowardBuyingCapability
EXPRESSION: DELTA(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(aqc, 0), 3), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(aqc, 0), 3), ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3)))), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: A firm that is actively shifting its investment program away from building plant and knowledge internally toward buying capability is making a strategy change that the market prices slowly, and such shifts predict lower returns beyond the standing level of acquisitiveness.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This abandons the gross-profit-scaling family entirely and instead isolates one specific design choice within the only mechanism in the archive that produced a reliable FF5 alpha: whether the buy-versus-build effect is a stable firm characteristic (level, tested by the accepted Signal 1) or a transition that arrives as news (change, tested here). Because it is a one-year change in a bounded three-year mix, it is not a function of R&D-reporting status the way the flagged capex-minus-R&D construction was, it retains full coverage through the coalesced acquisition and R&D legs, and a shift in mix leaves total investment scale roughly unchanged so it stays distinct from the level-of-investment sorts CMA neutralizes.
